private_notes.observations: In Q1, our $300 rate matched Birchwood Hale’s and was below Calder Rowe’s $325. We received 729 hours, generating $72,943 in profit. One quarter is insufficient to estimate how sensitive allocations are to price.

private_notes.observations: In Q1, our $300 rate yielded 729 hours and $72,943 in profit. The other firms charged $300 and $325. One quarter of data is insufficient to estimate how allocations respond to rate changes.

private_notes.observations: At $325 in Q1, Calder Rowe received 442 hours despite both competitors charging $300. The account generated about $55,300 in profit, but one quarter does not establish how sensitive allocations are to price.

Birchwood Hale also raised its rate to $315; Calder Rowe remained at $325. The data do not isolate the effect of our own rate from the panel-wide increase.

private_notes.observations: Raising our rate from $300 to $315 coincided with hours falling from 729 to 666, while quarterly profit rose from about $72,943 to $76,631.
